hints: Look for a chloride that does not exist as a simple molecule, but joins together with another copy of itself to become stable.
Recall that aluminium chloride exists as the dimer $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$, where an electron-deficient Al accepts a lone pair from a Cl on the neighbour.
Check $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{MgCl}_2$ for this behaviour, then pick the combination that leaves only the dimer-forming element.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the question needs**

Think like this: we need normal shared-electron covalent bonds PLUS a dative bond where one atom gives both electrons. This happens when molecules dimerise.

Rule to spot it:
$$\text{electron-deficient central atom + lone pair donor} \rightarrow \text{dative bond}$$

**Test 1, Al**

Aluminium chloride is electron deficient. $\text{Al}$ in $\text{AlCl}_3$ has only 6 electrons in its outer shell, so two $\text{AlCl}_3$ units join to form $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$.

In the dimer:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6 \text{ has 4 terminal Al-Cl covalent bonds + 2 bridging Al-Cl dative bonds}$$

**Test 2, Si and 3, Mg**

Silicon tetrachloride, $\text{SiCl}_4$, is a simple tetrahedral covalent molecule. Si already has a full octet, so it has no reason to dimerise, only normal covalent Si-Cl bonds.

Magnesium chloride, $\text{MgCl}_2$, is ionic with giant lattice structure. It has ionic bonding, not covalent plus dative, so it does not qualify.

**Conclude the combination**

Only statement 1 is correct. That matches the option for 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean Al, Si and Mg all qualify. SiCl4 is purely covalent and MgCl2 is ionic, so they do not show both covalent and dative bonding.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean Al and Si both qualify. Al does form Al2Cl6 with dative bonds, but Si forms only simple covalent SiCl4 with a complete octet and no dimerisation.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean Si and Mg qualify. Neither does. SiCl4 has only normal covalent bonds and MgCl2 is an ionic lattice.
options.D: Correct. Only Al qualifies. AlCl3 dimerises to Al2Cl6 to complete the octet on Al. The bridging Cl atoms use a lone pair to form a coordinate bond to the other Al, while all other bonds are normal covalent.
